children: Wall Street closed higher Friday as easing Treasury yields and lower oil prices supported equities, with investors continuing to monitor developments surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.
The blue-chip Dow
was up 0.9%, the benchmark S&P 500 (
) advanced 0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite
gained 0.4%.
The S&P 500 Health Care Sector Index
also gained 1.4% for the week.

Here are some of the important healthcare stories from this week:
Novo Nordisk shares slide 7% despite $23B obesity target, 2030 growth goals
Despite unveiling 2030 growth goals and a $23B obesity sales target, Novo Nordisk
saw its shares slide as much as 7% following its Capital Markets Day presentation in London on Monday.
The Wegovy-maker targets launching more than five multi-blockbusters by 2030 and aims to have at least five Phase 3 programs each in obesity/diabetes and other therapy areas.

Novo plans to scale capacity to serve 10x more people with obesity on oral GLP-1 by 2030, it said in a statement. The company aims to maintain a broadly stable adjusted operating margin and an attractive dividend per share through 2030.

CEO Mike Doustdar told investors that the “elephant in the room” was that semaglutide, the active ingredient in weight-loss and diabetes medicines Wegovy and Ozempic, will lose key patent exclusivity starting in the early next decade. It expires in 2032 in the U.S., which accounts for more than half of its sales.
This loss of exclusivity “is what’s on most people’s mind, and rightfully so,” Doustdar said, according to
CNBC
. “We created an incredibly attractive market, and now almost every other single pharma company, big or small, is trying to come and compete with us. We need to be ready for that,” he added.
Novo's
shares have plunged by more than 70% since its peak, while Lilly's
have surged.
Trump administration removes hundreds of thousands of Obamacare enrollees
Leading players operating in the marketplace for Affordable Care Act plans
on Tuesday after the Trump administration announced the removal of hundreds of thousands of people from the ACA public exchanges due to allegations of fraud.

The administration will also remove hundreds of brokers and agents who wrongly signed ACA enrollees for government healthcare, Vice President JD Vance and Dr. Mehmet Oz, the administrator for the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, said during a press conference on Tuesday.

Vance added that as part of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, the administration will end subsidy payments for 750,000 individual accounts in ACA exchanges, alleging their enrollments were unauthorized and fraudulent.

The purge is expected to target people who are unaware of their enrollments, earn an annual income exceeding 400% of the federal poverty level, or have employer-provided healthcare and are therefore ineligible for the program.

The CMS said in a statement that on August 31 it canceled about 315,000 ACA enrollments, affecting more than 760,000 individuals after confirming that their enrollments were unauthorized, an outcome it said will generate a $2.2B gain in advance payments of the premium tax credit.
Leading operators in the ACA Marketplace include UnitedHealth
, Centene
, Cigna
, Elevance Health
, Oscar Health
, and CVS Health
InnoCare inks licensing deal with Eli Lilly worth up to $3.35B
InnoCare Pharma
a research collaboration and license agreement with Eli Lilly
to develop new medicines, the companies said on Thursday.

InnoCare will leverage its drug discovery platform and research to discover and advance compounds against up to five targets. The company is eligible to receive up to $100M in upfront and near-term payments.
Milestone-based payments of up to $3.25B are contingent on development and commercial achievements.
InnoCare will also be eligible for single-digit tiered royalties based on annual net product sales.
Lilly wins FDA nod for once-weekly insulin product, Onswik
Eli Lilly
on Thursday announced that the U.S. FDA approved its once-weekly basal insulin product, Onswik, for adults with type 2 diabetes to be used with diet and exercise for the control of high blood sugar.

The decision is supported by data from the company’s QWINT Phase 3 clinical trials in which Onswik reached the primary endpoint, showing a comparable efficacy level to once-daily insulin products, insulin glargine U-100 (glargine), or insulin degludec U-100 (degludec).

According to the Indiana-based pharma giant, Onswik has the potential to cut more than 300 insulin injections annually compared with once-daily basal insulin. The decision marked the fourth global regulatory action favoring the product after similar approvals in Europe, Mexico, and Japan.
The company expects to launch Onswik in the coming months in two concentrations: 500 units/mL and 1,000 units/mL.
